subtitle: Common ground is useful, but it doesn’t settle everything. Learn to keep what you share with others while examining the meanings, circumstances and choices it leaves open.
scope: For staff across DHS. Minimization is an official IDC concept, not a label assigned by this course. Reflect privately or use the practice examples. No activity infers an individual’s IDI result, cultural identity or reason for personal choices. Actual access, employment, policy and records processes retain their appropriate roles. Matters involving Native American communities or Tribal relations should be referred to the person or area responsible within ADSA.
introTranscript: Common ground can help people connect. It can also end a needed question too early if a shared value or purpose is treated as proof that everyone means the same thing or faces the same conditions. This course explores Minimization through personal, group-learning and DHS service examples. You will keep what is useful about shared values while examining learned meanings, hidden defaults, choices about disclosure and relevant work conditions. The goal is richer understanding and appropriate action, without making difference a stereotype or placing people on the continuum.

intro.heading: Notice when common ground closes a question
intro.body:
Minimization is a concept in the official IDC concerning the way emphasis on commonality can obscure relevant difference. The learning issue is not that sharing a purpose or value is wrong. It is that a statement of similarity can be used as the complete answer before another meaning or condition has been considered. This course explores that issue through invented accounts rather than assessing people.

Practice Evie and Rory both value honesty. Evie learned that an honest conversation lets a person finish a thought before questions are asked. Rory learned that asking a direct question during the explanation demonstrates active, honest engagement. Saying “we both value honesty” does not explain why the same exchange felt respectful to one and interrupting to the other.

The shared value is still useful. They can ask what each action means in this conversation and agree on a suitable way to proceed. They need not prove a cultural group membership or decide which background is superior. The practice learned meanings are individual accounts, not predictions about people with similar names or affiliations.

Begin with what is shared, then name the question it leaves unresolved. In DHS work, a shared commitment to service also does not establish identical access circumstances. Relevant questions need their evidence and appropriate responsibility. A concept can guide inquiry without determining anyone’s IDI result or replacing an actual process.

flashcards.back: An official concept in which emphasis on similarity can obscure a deeper understanding of relevant difference; no personal placement is made here.
A purpose, concern or value people may share without necessarily interpreting it identically.
An understanding shaped by experience and context, which remains an individual account rather than a group rule.
An assumed arrangement presented as neutral without examining what it asks of different people.
A person’s decision about whether to join an activity or disclose something, not evidence of a cultural stage.
A meaning or condition that matters to the actual question and needs appropriate examination.
A claim tied to the evidence and setting actually examined, with other questions left open.

items.title: A shared word is a start
items.body: Honesty gives Evie and Rory a meaningful point of connection. It does not establish which conversational act each learned to experience as honest engagement. Retain the value and ask about its expression in the specific exchange, rather than dismissing the common ground or assuming its meaning is settled.

items.title: An unanswered meaning
items.body: Rory’s question during the explanation feels engaged to Rory and interrupting to Evie. The commonality statement does not answer that difference. A proportionate inquiry can make the meanings visible without an identity profile, a superiority claim or a demand that every future conversation use one fixed method.

items.title: The concept has limits
items.body: The invented exchange illustrates a learning question about commonality and difference. It does not establish either person’s orientation. Work examples also need their actual evidence and roles. Discuss what the statement overlooks rather than turning the concept into a shortcut to a personal assessment or formal determination.

tabs.label: Similarity as the whole answer
tabs.body: Similarity as the whole answer can end inquiry at “we both value honesty.” The exchange still contains different meanings of questions and respect. Ask what remains unresolved so the shared value helps conversation rather than conceals the condition that made the interaction difficult.

tabs.label: Reject all commonality
tabs.body: Rejecting all commonality loses a genuine connection and may create a false choice between similarity and difference. Evie and Rory can retain honesty as important and examine its expressions. The aim is a more nuanced account, not an assumption that people have nothing meaningful in common.

tabs.label: Common ground with inquiry
tabs.body: Common ground with inquiry keeps the value and asks about the actual meaning of the response. It can support a suitable conversation arrangement without ranking backgrounds. For work, the same approach also keeps the evidence and actual requirements visible rather than using a shared mission as proof that every condition is met.

check.question: Evie and Rory both value honesty but interpret a question during an explanation differently. What does the shared value establish?
check.correct: A useful common ground; the meaning of the conversational acts still needs appropriate inquiry.
wrong: Identical meanings of every action in the conversation.
Proof that one person is dishonest when an interpretation differs.
An actual IDI result for both people.
check.feedbackCorrect: The shared value supports connection while leaving the specific meanings open for understanding.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A shared word does not prove identical interpretations. A different meaning does not by itself establish dishonesty. The practice exchange does not administer the IDI. Retain the common ground and examine the act, context and expressed meaning without a personal or group verdict.

items.text: Both people in the example value honesty.
Both want a respectful conversation.
What does a question during an explanation mean to each?
Which arrangement would serve this exchange?
Shared honesty proves identical interpretation.
Different meanings determine an IDI result.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: Evie and Rory share honesty as a value, but their learned meanings of questions during a conversation differ.
options: Retain honesty as common ground and ask about the acts’ meanings in this exchange.
Declare one person dishonest because the meanings differ.

responses: This keeps connection and opens the relevant difference.
The different interpretation does not establish that moral conclusion.
The shared value does not settle the specific meaning or arrangement.

lessons.transfer: Use Evie and Rory or an invented exchange to identify common ground and one meaning it leaves unresolved.

move.control: You can keep a useful similarity without closing a needed question.
move.failure: A shared value becomes proof that everyone experiences the situation identically.
move.next: Ask what the commonality claim does not yet explain.

lessons.statement: Understand your own expression of a value while leaving room for another meaning.

intro.heading: Explore what a shared value means to you
intro.body:
Self-reflection can reveal why a common word feels obvious to you. Honesty, respect, connection or care may carry meanings learned through relationships, language, place and experience. A meaningful understanding is not fixed by one origin story. You can explore what the value means now without proving that one affiliation explains every response.

Evie recalls that listening to a complete account before questioning it expressed attention and respect in familiar conversations. Rory recalls that a thoughtful question during an account showed engagement. Neither invented experience establishes a universal group practice. It gives each person a starting meaning to examine and an opportunity to understand another expression.

Privately consider a broad value or use the practice pair. Ask what expression feels natural, what it means to you and whether its meaning has changed. You can leave the question open or choose the practice path without a judgment about commitment or cultural development.

The result may be a more nuanced personal account, not an action plan. That is worthwhile without a work metric. Connect the learning to work when useful, but do not turn personal reflection into a required private history or evidence for a personnel decision. Retain the value while questioning whether its familiar expression is the only possible one.

items.title: Value and expression
items.body: Evie values honesty and associates listening through a full explanation with respectful attention. Separating those ideas allows her to retain the value while considering a different expression. It does not require declaring the learned practice wrong or assuming every person shares its meaning.

items.title: Meaning can change
items.body: Rory may come to see that a question felt engaged to Rory but disruptive in this particular exchange. That insight need not erase the value of active inquiry. It can deepen personal understanding of when and how a familiar expression fits, without claiming a complete cause of the preference.

items.title: Choice about reflection
items.body: A learner may reflect privately on a broad value or use Evie and Rory. Neither a detailed personal account nor a workplace result is required. If sharing is chosen, keep it comfortable and nonsensitive rather than making disclosure quantity the measure of cultural authenticity or competence.

tabs.label: One expression as the value itself
tabs.body: Treating one expression as the value itself may make another response seem morally deficient. Evie can distinguish honesty from uninterrupted listening, and Rory can distinguish honesty from immediate questioning. That distinction broadens meaning without deciding that every expression is equally suitable in every context.

tabs.label: Discard the meaningful experience
tabs.body: Discarding the experience entirely can make learning feel like rejection of what mattered to you. A familiar expression can remain valuable in a suitable setting. Reflection asks where its meaning and limits are, not whether your whole background must be judged inferior to become open to another account.

tabs.label: Personal meaning with room
tabs.body: Personal meaning with room recognizes the learned expression and asks what another account may reveal. The reflection can stay private and unfinished. It does not need an operational product or public demonstration of insight, and it cannot predict another person’s behavior from an affiliation.

check.question: Which personal reflection fits the course?
check.correct: Explore what honesty means to Evie or Rory and distinguish it from one familiar expression, privately or practicely, without requiring a work result.
wrong: Require everyone to share a private family history.
Treat a different expression as proof that the other person has no values.
Accept reflection only when a work metric changes.
check.feedbackCorrect: The reflection values personal meaning and inquiry while preserving choice and avoiding a universal or instrumental-only claim.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A private family history is unnecessary. A different expression does not prove a lack of values. Personal reflection need not change a work metric to matter. Choose a meaningful question and examine its expression privately or through the example, without an identity or disclosure test.

items.text: Evie explores why listening through an explanation feels respectful.
Rory considers what immediate questioning has meant in familiar conversation.
The learner uses the practice pair rather than sharing an account.
How might the meaning change in another setting?
Every person with the same affiliation must use the same expression.
A work metric is required for personal insight to count.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A learner wants to privately explore a meaning of respect but a facilitator requests a detailed public history and a work action.

Meaningful private or practice reflection; the person chooses whether to share it or apply it at work.
An authenticity score based on the account.

This respects personal understanding as a worthwhile outcome and keeps choice genuine.
The activity cannot assess authenticity or developmental placement.

lessons.transfer: Privately explore a broad value and one familiar expression, or use Evie and Rory. No personal account needs to be entered.

move.control: You can deepen personal understanding and decide whether anything is shared.
move.failure: A universal or work-proof rule replaces meaningful reflection.
move.next: Separate the value from a single expression of it.

intro.heading: Examine the default inside a shared-purpose activity
intro.body:
“We all want connection” may be a useful statement, but it does not establish how everyone experiences one activity. A familiar method can be presented as neutral while asking for a particular kind of personal sharing. Examine the arrangement itself rather than treating the common aim as evidence that it fits everyone.

In a practice staff learning session, an organizer plans a round of personal family stories because connection is a shared aim. Some learners prefer a practice example or private reflection. The organizer reads that choice as resistance to belonging. The choice does not establish that motive. The activity can retain a meaningful aim while allowing other appropriate ways to participate.

A genuine alternative is available without demanding the personal reason for using it. Say plainly that each person chooses whether to share, provide a practice route and avoid grading the depth of private disclosure. A supervisor’s role can add pressure, so make the boundary clear rather than rely on a casual statement that no one has to share.

This does not mean people can opt out of required work tasks. Identify whether the activity is personal reflection or an actual responsibility, and use the process that applies when a formal need or requirement is involved. Do not convert a cultural learning activity into a compulsory identity profile or use a shared value to remove real protections and choices.

items.title: Aim and method are different
items.body: Connection names a purpose. A personal-story round is one chosen method, not proof that the purpose is served for everyone. Examine what the method asks learners to reveal and which suitable alternatives are possible, rather than diagnosing someone who does not choose the familiar route.

items.title: Authority can add pressure
items.body: When a supervisor asks for stories, a learner may feel that declining will affect how belonging or commitment is judged. Clarify the optional boundary and avoid collecting reasons for the choice. The practice route should be accepted as genuine participation, without a hidden disclosure score.

items.title: Keep real responsibilities distinct
items.body: A personal-reflection activity is different from a required work task or an authorized process. Preserve that distinction. Appropriate alternatives to a learning disclosure do not cancel actual duties, and actual duties do not automatically justify asking for a private family or cultural history in the course.

tabs.label: Shared aim as proof
tabs.body: Using the shared aim as proof can make every concern about the method seem like resistance. The organizer may overlook the disclosure burden. Retain the connection goal and inspect the participation route instead of treating the value as a reason no further question is allowed.

tabs.label: Alternative with a disclosure gate
tabs.body: An alternative that requires a private reason is not a genuine choice. It asks the learner to disclose in order to avoid disclosure. Provide a practice route without a justification test, and keep genuine formal needs in their appropriate processes rather than improvising a learning gate.

tabs.label: Purpose with genuine choice
tabs.body: Purpose with genuine choice allows personal sharing, private reflection or practice where appropriate. The organizer can support connection without a compulsory story. State the boundary clearly and avoid assigning commitment or an IDC orientation from how much a learner chooses to reveal.

check.question: The practice story activity aims to support connection. Which response preserves purpose and choice?
check.correct: Provide a genuine private or practice route without requiring a personal reason or scoring disclosure; keep actual work duties distinct.
wrong: Treat the shared aim as proof that everyone must share a family story.
Require a private reason to access the practice route.
Infer an IDI orientation from a learner’s choice.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response examines the method independently of the shared purpose and makes the optional boundary genuine.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A shared aim does not make personal disclosure necessary. A private-reason gate undermines the alternative. A participation choice cannot establish an IDI result. Retain the purpose, provide an appropriate genuine route and distinguish personal learning from actual duties without labeling the learner.

items.text: Support connection in the learning session.
Invite meaningful reflection on experience.
Offer a practice account without requiring a private reason.
Allow personal reflection to remain private.
Declining a story proves resistance to belonging.
A private history is required to use the alternative.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: An invented staff learning activity uses personal stories for connection and judges learners who choose a practice alternative.
options: Make every personal story mandatory because the aim is shared.

Retain the aim and make private or practice reflection a genuine option without a hidden judgment.
responses: The purpose does not establish that compulsory sharing is necessary or suitable.
The gate reproduces the disclosure demand.
This keeps the learning purpose while respecting a relevant participation difference.

lessons.transfer: Examine an invented shared-purpose activity for its participation demands and a genuine alternative route.

move.control: You can make the activity’s assumed method and each person’s choices visible.
move.failure: A common aim hides a compulsory disclosure method.
move.next: Separate the purpose from what the arrangement asks people to reveal.

lessons.statement: Respect the choice and do not make silence or sameness a complete account.

intro.heading: Respect a person’s choice without inferring its cause
intro.body:
A person may use common language, agree with a shared aim or leave a difference unspoken. That does not show everything the person understands or experiences. The official account of Minimization notes that emphasis on commonality can have different functions, including navigating practices set by a more dominant setting. This course does not infer which function applies to any learner or colleague.

In the practice story activity, a learner says that connection matters and chooses the example. The organizer could assume the person has no meaningful difference, is resisting openness or is concealing something specific. None is established. The learner’s choice can be respected without a complete explanation.

If a relevant work question remains, ask about that question through a suitable route. Do not require the person to reveal an identity or private experience to establish that the question is legitimate. For personal learning, the person can reflect privately, use an example or leave a prompt aside without a developmental verdict.

This is not a rule to ignore all uncertainty or formal needs. Actual access and work concerns use their appropriate process and evidence. The learning boundary is that a chosen expression, agreement or silence does not diagnose a person’s orientation, history or motivation. Keep curiosity proportionate and personal meaning voluntary.

Explain why shared language may not reveal everything a person experiences.

What response is appropriate?
lessons.keyStatement: Respect the choice and do not make silence or sameness a complete account.

items.title: Shared words have a limit
items.body: Connection matters identifies a stated value, not the learner’s full account of belonging. It may be a sincere shared aim while other meanings remain private. Respect the statement without requiring the learner to disclose a hidden difference or treating the words as proof that every condition is identical.

items.title: Choice does not establish motive
items.body: The learner’s use of fiction is observable. Resistance, fear or an assumed coping strategy would be added interpretations unless the person chooses to explain them. Do not turn the official model’s conceptual possibilities into diagnoses of a particular employee. A genuine optional route needs no such verdict.

items.title: Ask the actual question
items.body: If an instruction is unclear, ask what part needs clarification. If the question belongs in an access or formal process, use it. A work need should not require a private cultural account as its evidence, and a personal learning choice should not be treated as a formal personnel assessment.

tabs.label: Assume full sameness
tabs.body: Assuming full sameness may take agreement with a value as proof that no different meaning or circumstance exists. The statement supplies only its chosen scope. Leave room for another appropriate question without forcing a private explanation or inventing what must be hidden.

tabs.label: Infer the hidden reason
tabs.body: Inferring the hidden reason can look perceptive while imposing a story the learner did not choose. A model may describe possibilities, but the course cannot determine an individual’s motive or orientation. Respect the choice and keep actual task questions separate from a speculative biography.

tabs.label: Respect chosen scope
tabs.body: Respecting chosen scope accepts the value and participation choice as stated. Use a relevant inquiry when a work question needs examination, and keep optional meaning voluntary. This approach leaves space for difference without diagnosing silence or treating similarity as proof that every lived experience is the same.

check.question: A learner endorses connection and chooses the practice example. What can the organizer soundly conclude?
check.correct: The learner stated a shared aim and selected an available route; the choice does not establish motive, hidden experience or an IDI orientation.
wrong: The choice proves the person has no different experiences.
The choice proves a particular cultural coping strategy.
The person must disclose a private reason before the route is accepted.
check.feedbackCorrect: The conclusion respects the expressed scope and avoids converting model possibilities into a personal diagnosis or disclosure gate.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A stated shared aim does not reveal all experience. A practice choice does not prove a coping strategy or cultural stage. A private-reason requirement undermines optionality. Describe the stated choice, respect its scope and use appropriate work processes only for relevant actual questions.

items.text: The learner says connection matters.
The learner selects the practice example.
No private reason is required to use this alternative route.
Which actual instruction needs clarification, if any?
The choice proves no cultural difference exists.
The choice proves a specific hidden coping motive.

options: Accept the stated choice and ask only a relevant task question if needed, without inferring motive or placement.
Assign a cultural stage because the choice fits a possible model pattern.
Require private disclosure to disprove the organizer’s interpretation.
responses: This preserves choice and keeps inquiry within the account actually available.
A conceptual possibility does not establish an individual assessment result.

lessons.transfer: Use an invented participation choice to separate the stated fact, an added inference and the boundary that should be respected.

move.control: You can avoid assigning a private meaning to another person’s choice.
move.failure: Shared language or silence is treated as either complete sameness or a hidden diagnosis.
move.next: State what the choice shows and what it does not establish.

intro.heading: Keep a service mission and examine access conditions
intro.body:
A common service mission can motivate staff across DHS, but does not answer how a particular instruction or route works for people with different circumstances. Everyone wants clear information is a useful aim. The same notice was sent to everyone is an activity fact. Neither establishes that the notice was understandable and usable in every relevant situation.

In a practice service-information review, a team uses the same internal terminology in every notice because it believes consistency ensures fairness. Some reviewed examples show uncertainty about the next contact. Examine the specific wording and route rather than assume that the same document produces the same result. Do not invent a person’s language, disability or cultural need from identity.

A proportionate step could clarify the terminology and appropriate contact within the responsible process. Other language, format or access questions may need their established routes and suitable evidence. Keep unexamined conditions unknown. This course creates no program eligibility rule, universal translation promise or new accommodation policy.

For an actual decision, follow the applicable agency equity analysis, tools, records and decision responsibilities. The course routine is preparation. Staff can develop the work with consultant guidance and feedback without requiring consultant permission for every resource use. A supported recommendation describes purpose, affected circumstances, evidence, limitations and the proper next responsibility.

Identify an actual condition a practice identical-method claim leaves unexamined.
Choose a bounded inquiry or action through the appropriate work responsibility.
What should the team do?
lessons.keyStatement: Retain the common purpose and examine whether the arrangement serves it.

items.title: Intent, activity and result
items.body: The team wants fairness and sends the same notice. Those describe intent and activity. A result question asks whether people can use the information for its actual purpose. Keep these distinctions visible so a positive aim or consistent distribution does not become unsupported reassurance about universal access.

items.title: A specific examined gap
items.body: The reviewed practice examples cannot locate the next contact because terms are unexplained. Clarify the relevant instruction and appropriate route. The action follows the observed gap rather than a guessed group need. It does not establish that every possible access question has been answered.

items.title: Other conditions need appropriate evidence
items.body: A remaining format or language question should use its proper process and information. Do not guess what a person needs or promise a service the actual program does not provide. Keep the unknown visible and develop a responsible next inquiry rather than treating the shared mission as a completed analysis.

tabs.label: Same method as proof
tabs.body: The same method can support consistency but does not itself prove usability. The notice may still contain an unclear term or route. Ask what evidence examines its actual purpose, and retain the shared mission without using sameness to close an access question prematurely.

tabs.label: Difference as guesswork
tabs.body: Difference as guesswork assigns needs from identity instead of the actual account. That can stereotype people and create an inappropriate response. Examine expressed needs and suitable evidence through the relevant process, rather than assuming all people in a category need the same method.

tabs.label: Purpose and conditions together
tabs.body: Purpose and conditions together retain fairness as the aim while examining the instruction, route and actual evidence. A bounded clarification can be useful, with remaining questions appropriately owned. This supports practical equity work without inventing policy, a personal score or an assurance that every barrier is gone.

check.question: The practice team sends the same notice to everyone. What should the review examine?
check.correct: Whether the wording and route are usable for the actual purpose, using suitable evidence and appropriate processes while keeping other conditions unknown.
wrong: Assume identical distribution proves universal access.
Guess each person’s need from a cultural or disability label.
Treat the course as permission to create eligibility or language-assistance rules independently.
check.feedbackCorrect: The review separates mission and activity from an evidence-supported result and preserves actual policy and decision responsibility.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Identical distribution does not prove universal access. Labels cannot determine an individual need. The course does not create eligibility or language-assistance authority. Retain the service purpose, examine the actual condition through suitable evidence and routes, and state the remaining unknowns before a real recommendation is finalized.

lessons.statement: Keep the connection and the clearer question, with its limits intact.

intro.heading: Review commonality and difference without a stage claim
intro.body:
A course result may be a more nuanced personal meaning. Evie and Rory can see that honesty matters to both while its familiar expressions differ. A learner may privately recognize the same distinction in a chosen value or use the practice example. This is worthwhile understanding even without public sharing or operational proof.

A work result has its own evidence. The practice notice review now distinguishes common mission, identical distribution and the unexamined usability question. A clarification might improve the examples checked, but other access conditions remain open. Describe the gain and limit rather than declare that all inequity disappeared when the team reconsidered sameness.

Neither result determines an IDI orientation. The official IDC has five orientations ending with Adaptation. In this program, Integration means the people a process affects help design it; it is not an extra official orientation. Shared language, private choices, correct answers and an improved instruction cannot place a person on the continuum.

Choose another question that fits your purpose. You can explore a personal meaning privately, use an invented activity or develop an actual work inquiry through its suitable process. The consultant offers guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff build their capability and prepare their work. Keep common ground useful and relevant differences examinable, rather than making either one the complete account of people.

inThisLesson: Describe a personal-understanding or bounded work gain from examining commonality.
Identify what remains unknown without inferring someone’s experience.
Choose a further inquiry without an IDI placement or a disclosure requirement.
Which review is sound?
lessons.keyStatement: Keep the connection and the clearer question, with its limits intact.

items.title: A more nuanced personal meaning
items.body: Evie can retain honesty as important and recognize another learned expression without ranking Rory or rejecting her own experience. A learner may keep a similar insight private. The meaning remains open to further reflection and does not require a work product or proof of cultural authenticity.

items.title: A work result with scope
items.body: The team’s inquiry now asks whether the notice serves the actual information need. That is a reasoning gain. If the changed notice has not been used, its operational effect remains unknown. Keep the shared purpose and evidence limits clear instead of using the course result as a universal assurance.

items.title: Another appropriate question
items.body: A new question may concern a value, a participation choice or a work condition. Choose suitable evidence and boundaries for the path. Do not infer an individual’s hidden meaning or IDC placement from the answer, and retain actual formal duties rather than treating continuing learning as a substitute.

tabs.label: Commonality alone
tabs.body: Commonality alone can leave the learner with a useful value but an incomplete account of its meanings and conditions. Retain the connection and ask what remains to understand. The aim is not to stop sharing values, but to prevent similarity from functioning as unsupported reassurance.

tabs.label: Difference alone
tabs.body: Difference alone can erase genuine connection or encourage identity predictions. Keep individual accounts and context central while recognizing the shared purpose. A relevant distinction should improve understanding or inquiry, not require a stereotype, private biography or denial that people can share something meaningful.

tabs.label: Connection and bounded inquiry
tabs.body: Connection and bounded inquiry keep the shared value or mission and the question it does not settle. Personal understanding can remain private; work claims keep their evidence and responsibilities. This supports continued development without a hidden orientation score or an assumption that one course resolves every barrier.

check.question: Which review preserves the course’s learning and limits?
check.correct: Describe the useful common ground, the meaning or condition now better understood and the remaining question, without a personal placement or work-proof gate for private growth.
wrong: Declare that every participant’s Minimization is permanently eliminated.
Infer a person’s hidden experience from agreement or silence.
Value only reflections that produce measured operational change.
check.feedbackCorrect: The review keeps connection and the relevant inquiry together while respecting personal growth, evidence scope and assessment limits.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Course completion cannot guarantee a permanent assessment change. Agreement or silence does not reveal a hidden experience. Private personal growth does not require operational metrics. Name the connection and clearer question, retain what remains unknown and choose a further inquiry without a personal stage or disclosure test.

items.text: The practice pair distinguishes shared honesty from identical expression.
The notice review separates mission, distribution and result.
Other access conditions have not been examined.
What personal meaning does the learner want to explore privately next?
Completion guarantees a particular IDI orientation.
A private insight has value only if a work metric changes.

lessons.next: Keep common ground useful, personal meanings voluntary and actual conditions open to appropriate examination.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A learner gains a private insight into a shared value and a team in this example improves its access questions. A facilitator wants to declare everyone’s cultural stage changed.
options: Use correct answers to assign orientations.
Count only the team’s operational metrics as legitimate learning.
Recognize personal understanding and bounded work inquiry, retain questions and keep actual assessment separate.
responses: Correct answers do not administer the IDI or establish placement.
Personal cultural growth is also legitimate without operational proof.
This values the learning paths while preserving evidence and assessment boundaries.

lessons.transfer: Privately review a value or use Evie and Rory; if useful, describe a work gain and its scope. Choose another inquiry without entering sensitive material.

move.control: You can preserve shared purpose and an open question without a personal score.
move.failure: The result becomes total reassurance, a hidden diagnosis or an instrumental-only test.
move.next: Name the connection, the relevant difference and one further question.

jobAid.subtitle: Keep shared values and purposes while examining the meanings and conditions they do not settle.
remember: A shared value does not prove identical expression or experience.
Private reflection and practice are legitimate without entered notes or work metrics.
The course cannot infer motive, hidden experience or an IDI orientation from a choice.

sections.heading: Start with connection
items: Name the useful common ground without treating it as the complete answer.
Explore a learned meaning privately or through Evie and Rory.
Distinguish a value from one familiar expression.

sections.heading: Examine the arrangement
items: Ask what the shared-purpose method requires from people.
Make private or practice participation genuinely available without asking for a reason.
For work, examine the actual condition with appropriate evidence and responsibility.
Do not assign needs or motives from identity, agreement or silence.

sections.heading: Review and continue
items: Recognize a more nuanced personal understanding as a valid outcome.
State work gains with their actual scope and remaining unknowns.
Use actual agency analysis and formal routes for required decisions.
Choose a further inquiry with consultant guidance available and staff ownership retained.

sources.title: Intercultural Development Inventory: official IDC overview
sources.note: Primary source for Minimization and the official five-orientation model, including different conceptual functions of commonality. No function, orientation or hidden motive is inferred for an individual, and no IDI items are reproduced.

sources.title: Council of Europe: Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: Explores varied meanings, multiple affiliations, reflection and appropriate inquiry. The personal and DHS activities were developed for this course, not copied from the source or required as private inventories.

sources.title: UNESCO Universal Declaration on Cultural Diversity
sources.note: Conceptual cultural-diversity context with human-dignity boundaries. It is not used to create a new Minnesota participation, service or operational mandate.

sources.title: DHS Equity Policy
sources.note: Actual agency equity-learning, analysis, tools and decision responsibilities remain applicable. Required work continues, and course routines do not authorize new eligibility or access policies.
